title: Commit cushion & slab slippage lab — Q4 2026
content:
Purpose:
Quick, parametric sheet to estimate how slab-commit cushions and a GPU spot-price slippage event interact with hiring glidepaths and per-token price break-even. This is an internal lab — lean, reproducible, and intended for conversation with Product and SRE before a consolidated ask to Exec.

High-level summary (one line):
If spot GPU costs spike 40% while committed-slab utilization drops 10ppt (due to customer churn or slower trial conversion), we need to either raise per-token price by ~12–18% or defer ~12 FTEs in the next 12 months to keep margin targets.

Assumptions (editable):
- Baseline date: Nov-2026.
- Baseline hosted unit economics (derived from internal chargeback): average cost-per-token (CPT) = $0.00060 (includes infra, amortized model license, infra overhead).
- Baseline blended token mix: chat: 62%, embeddings: 28%, reranking/other: 10%. Effective revenue-net-per-token (RPT) = $0.00120 (after discounts).
- Target gross margin on hosted = 50% (pre-S&M/ops).
- Average engineer fully-burdened cost = $240k/year. Average ramp to productive = 3 months.
- GPU exposure bucket: 65% committed, 35% spot (regionally diversified).
- Slab cushion definition: committed headroom we keep unallocated to smooth bursts; current cushion = 12% of committed capacity.

Key variables (sheet columns in the quick model):
- Spot cost shock (%) — delta to spot GPU unit hourly rate.
- Slab-utilization drop (ppt) — percent-point reduction in committed utilization (e.g., 12% -> 0.12 absolute).
- Token mix shift (ppt) — move to more expensive embeddings or longer-chat sequences.
- Headcount glidepath (FTE delta next 12 months) — hires paused or accelerated.
- Per-token price adjustment (%) — revenue price level change.

Scenario matrix (selected rows from the full sheet):
Columns: Scenario name | Spot shock | Slab-util-drop | Token-mix shift | HC glidepath vs plan | Required price change to preserve margin
Row A (baseline) | 0% | 0 ppt | 0 ppt | +0 FTE | 0%
Row B (mild shock) | +20% | 5 ppt | +3 ppt embeddings | -6 FTE (defer) | +6%
Row C (moderate shock) | +40% | 10 ppt | +6 ppt embeddings | -12 FTE (defer) | +12–14%
Row D (severe shock + clamp) | +70% | 18 ppt | +12 ppt embeddings/long chats | -20 FTE (defer) | +22–28% or accept margin drop

Selected numeric worked example (Row C):
- Baseline CPT = $0.00060. Spot bucket increases contribution to CPT by 40% * 35% = 14% CPI uplift (approx).
- Slab-util drop (10 ppt) increases per-token amortized committed cost by ~8% (fewer tokens amortizing fixed committed expense).
- Combined cost uplift ≈ 22%. New CPT ≈ $0.00060 * 1.22 = $0.000732.
- To keep 50% gross margin at same RPT of $0.00120 we need CPT <= $0.00060. If CPT = $0.000732 then required RPT = CPT / (1 - 0.5) = $0.001464 -> price delta ≈ +22% from baseline RPT.
- But partial mitigation via deferring hires: saving 12 FTEs = 12 * $240k = $2.88M/year (~$240k/month). If we allocate 30% of those savings against hosted CPT, effective offset is ~6–9% on blended CPT (back-of-envelope), lowering required price increase to ~12–14%.

Break-even levers (order of operational preference tested in lab):
1) Short-term: rebalance spot/committed mix by shifting ~10% of burst load to committed pools (if available) — reduces spot exposure quickly but may require small burst commit purchases.
2) Tactical: apply a targeted price increase for high-cost routes (long-chat premium + embeddings add-on) — route-level increases hit churn less than a platform-wide raise.
3) HR: pause non-critical hiring and freeze 50% of open roles in Q1 2027 — defers cash but impacts roadmap.
4) Product: tighten caching and KV prefix heuristics to reduce token consumption on high-cost flows (expected token reduction: 3–6% in heavy-chat apps).
5) Sales: temporarily throttle promotional slab discounts to new enterprise trials (reduces slab-utilization drop risk).

Sensitivity outputs included in sheet (visible in separate pivot tabs):
- Price delta sensitivity surface: X axis = spot shock (0–80%), Y axis = slab-util drop (0–20ppt). Values show price % change to restore margin.
- HC-savings equivalence table: maps deferred FTE count -> equivalent price delta reduction.
- Route-level elasticity assumptions (draft): embeddings elasticity = low (0.8), chat elasticity = moderate (1.4) — used to estimate churn impact from per-route price edits.

Open questions / uncertainties we should model next:
- How much of the slab-util drop is structural (customer churn) vs. timing (trial seasonality)? We need per-customer cohort usage profiles (ask CS for top 20).
- Can SRE provision short-term committed capacity in us-west-2 within 4 weeks at modest term? (ask infra/partnerships).
- Validate elasticity estimates with product A/B tests for a small subset of customers before broad price action.
- Confirm whether enterprise contracts have minimum token floors that legally limit per-route price changes mid-contract.

Actions / recommended next steps (owner in parens):
- Run per-customer slab-utilization time series for last 9 months and surface top 20 risk accounts (Priya Raman).
- Build A/B plan for targeted embedding premium on 5 mid-market customers (Julian Ortega + Solutions Eng).
- Ask Infra to produce a quick quote on a 6–12 month committed addendum to absorb 10% more burst (Marcus Liu).
- Re-run the sheet with vendor GPU spot market forward curves if available (Finance data team).

Appendix: compact quick calc (pasteable rows)
- Inputs: baseline CPT, spot-share, committed-share, spot-shock %, slab-util-drop %, FTE savings, average FTE cost, baseline RPT.
- Formula notes: cost-uplift_from_spot = spot-share * spot-shock. cost-uplift_from_util = function(slider) approximated as slab-util-drop * (committed-fixed-cost / baseline-token-volume-share).
- Suggested conservative guardrails: if model suggests >15% price lift to preserve margin, escalate to Exec for re-prioritization (pricing > +15% is high-risk).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative in modeling amortized committed costs and assumes linear elasticity. The sheet supports toggling to a cohort-level amortization where appropriate.
- We want to keep decisions modular: prefer route-level mitigations first, then HR, then platform-wide price changes.
